extra.reason:
Fixed in 4f2de01 and verified on real hardware 2026-07-28 00:07.

Root cause: when a monitor renegotiated resolution mid-run, setup-monitor correctly aborted with exit code 75, but monitor-watcher's reconcile loop then timed out instead of retrying, because start_time was set once before the loop while reap_setup had just cleared setup_pid. setup-monitor therefore never reached its fluxbox restart, so _NET_DESKTOP_GEOMETRY kept a stale value (6720x2160 for an 8000x2160 screen) and xfce4-notifyd placed notifications at +0+0.

Verified by replugging the Odyssey G75F, which reproduced the exact renegotiation (640x480 -> 3440x1440 -> 5120x2160) and the STALE abort, then showed the new 'Setup aborted as stale; waiting for new state to settle (retry 1/3)' path relaunching setup-monitor, which completed with exit code 0. _NET_DESKTOP_GEOMETRY is now 8000x2160 and notifications land correctly.

The nm-applet icon symptom originally filed here has a different cause and is split out as dc-9l7.

Fixed in audio repo commit 0ca9704 plus an edit to ~/.network-handler.d/mute (untracked by any repo).

Root cause: PipeWire has no master volume. Each sink holds its own mute state
and @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ is an alias resolved at use time, so muting the
default sink is undone whenever the default moves - which plugging in a
monitor reliably causes, since the new DisplayPort audio sink becomes default
and is unmuted.

Fix: wpvol gains mute-all/unmute-all, acting on every sink that can make
noise in the room (the machine's speaker plus all HDMI/DisplayPort outputs,
since monitors may have speakers). USB DACs and Bluetooth are left alone as
deliberately-chosen outputs. ~/.network-handler.d/mute now calls these
instead of the single-sink mute/unmute.

Verified end to end: invoking the handler with 'Ocean 23456' unmutes all five
sinks, and with 'L39-Member' mutes all five. Whichever sink becomes default
after a later monitor plug is therefore already muted.

Accepted trade-off: wired headphones are not a separate sink on this
hardware - plugging them in switches the device profile (Speaker ->
Headphones) and reuses the same sink node, so they are muted too. Adam
confirmed he does not use wired headphones.

Also fixed a latent bug in wpvol: getvol() kept only the volume level via
awk '{print $2}', discarding the MUTED marker, so 'getvol | grep -q MUTED'
could never match and MUTE_STATE was always 'no'. Affected only the bar()
display, since mute()/unmute() call wpctl set-mute directly.
